title: The Concept of Childhood in Western Countries

parts.title: Section 1
parts.passageHtml:
{[The history of childhood has been a heated topic in social history since the highly influential book Centuries of Childhood’, written by French historian Philippe Aries, emerged in 1960.][165986]} {[He claimed that ‘childhood’ is a concept created by modern society.][166015]}

{[Whether childhood is itself a recent invention has been one of the most intensely debated issues in the history of childhood.][166027]} {[Historian Philippe Aries asserted that children were regarded as miniature adults, with all the intellect and personality that this implies, in Western Europe during the Middle Ages (up to about the end of the 15th century).][166048]} {[After scrutinising medieval pictures and diaries, he concluded that there was no distinction between children and adults for they shared similar leisure activities and work; However, this does not mean children were neglected, forsaken or despised, he argued.][166087]} {[The idea of childhood corresponds to awareness about the peculiar nature of childhood, which distinguishes the child from adult, even the young adult.][166125]} {[Therefore, the concept of childhood is not to be confused with affection for children.][166149]}

{[Traditionally, children played a functional role in contributing to the family income in the history.][166165]} {[Under this circumstance, children were considered to be useful.][166179]} {[Back in the Middle Ages, children of 5 or 6 years old did necessary chores for their parents.][166189]} {[During the 16th century, children of 9 or 10 years old were often encouraged or even forced to leave their family to work as servants for wealthier families or apprentices for a trade.][166205]}

{[In the 18th and 19th centuries, industrialisation created a new demand for child labour; thus many children were forced to work for a long time in mines, workshops and factories.][166236]} {[The issue of whether long hours of labouring would interfere with children’s growing bodies began to perplex social reformers.][166265]} {[Some of them started to realise the potential of systematic studies to monitor how far these early deprivations might be influencing children’s development.][166285]}

{[The concerns of reformers gradually had some impact upon the working condition of children.][166311]} {[For example, in Britain, the Factory Act of 1833 signified the emergence of legal protection of children from exploitation and was also associated with the rise of schools for factory children.][166327]} {[Due partly to factory reform, the worst forms of child exploitation were eliminated gradually.][166359]} {[The influence of trade unions and economic changes also contributed to the evolution by leaving some forms of child labour redundant during.][166374]} {[Initiating children into work as ‘useful’ children was no longer a priority, and childhood was deemed to be a time for play and education for all childreninstead of a privileged minority.][166397]} {[Childhood was increasingly understood as a more extended phase of dependency, development and learning with the delay of the age for starting full-time work- Even so, work continued to play a significant, if less essential, role in children’s lives in the later 19th and 20th centuries.][166426]} {[Finally, the ‘useful child’ has become a controversial concept during the first decade of the 21st century, especially in the context of global concern about large numbers of children engaged in child labour.][166471]}

{[The half-time schools established upon the Factory Act of 1833 allowed children to work and attend school.][166505]} {[However, a significant proportion of children never attended school in the 1840s, and even if they did, they dropped out by the age of 10 or 11.][166523]} {[By the end of the 19th century in Britain, the situation changed dramatically, and schools became the core to the concept of a ‘normal’ childhood.][166549]}

{[It is no longer a privilege for children to attend school and all children are expected to spend a significant part of their day in a classroom.][166575]} {[Once in school, children’s lives could be separated from domestic life and the adult world of work.][166600]} {[In this way, school turns into an institution dedicated to shaping the minds, behaviour and morals of the young.][166618]} {[Besides, education dominated the management of children’s waking hours through the hours spent in the classroom, homework (the growth of ‘after school’ activities), and the importance attached to parental involvement.][166637]}

{[Industrialisation, urbanization and mass schooling pose new challenges for those who are responsible for protecting children’s welfare, as well as promoting their learning.][166669]} {[An increasing number of children are being treated as a group with unique needs, and are organized into groups in the light of their age.][166694]} {[For instance, teachers need to know some information about what to expect of children in their classrooms, what kinds of instruction are appropriate for different age groups, and what is the best way to assess children’s progress.][166718]} {[Also, they want tools enabling them to sort and select children according to their abilities and potential.][166756]}

questionSets.instructionHtml:
Questions 1 - 7:

Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?
In boxes 1-7 on your answer sheet, write:

TRUE               if the statement is true

FALSE              if the statement is false

NOT GIVEN    if the information is not given in the passage

questions.text: Aries pointed out that children did different types of work to adults during the Middle Ages.
questions.explanationHtml:
Đáp án "FALSE"

Aries cho rằng vào thời Middle Ages ở châu Châu, children được là người lớn mini (miniature adults)

Câu sau giải thích rõ ra tại sao ổng có kết luận đó:
+ sau khi xem pictures và diaries, Aries kết luận rằng nó ko có sự khác biệt giữa children và adults bởi vì (for) children và adults có hoạt động giải trí và công việc 

share sth: có cái gì giống như ai đó
Ex: My mom and I share the same passion for cooking.

=> câu hỏi nói children làm những công việc khác adults => ngược với thông tin trong bài

questions.text: Working children during the Middle Ages were generally unloved.
questions.explanationHtml:
Đáp án "False"

việc children được xem như là người lớn mini không có nghĩa là children bị bỏ bê, bỏ rơi hay bị ghét

questions.text: Some scientists thought that overwork might damage the health of young children.
questions.explanationHtml:
Đáp án "TRUE"

The issue began to perplex social reformers. Họ nhận ra tiềm năng của việc dùng nghiên cứu để xem coi là these early deprivations (đang trỏ đến việc "working for a long time" khi còn nhỏ) ảnh hưởng như thế nào đến sự phát triển của trẻ em

questions.text: The rise of trade unions majorly contributed to the protection of children from exploitation in the 19th century.
questions.explanationHtml:
Đáp án " NOT GIVEN"

trong bài chỉ nói trade unions và  economic changes góp phần vào thôi
trong bài KO đề cập cái nào thì góp phần nhiều (MAJORLY contributed) như trong câu hỏi

questions.text: the aid of half-time schools, most children went to school in the mid-19th century.
questions.explanationHtml:
Đáp án "FALSE"

- half-time schools thành lập với mục đích là có phép học sinh đi làm và đi học
- tuy nhiên 1 tỉ lệ lớn học sinh chưa bao giờ đi học hoặc nghỉ học sớm.

questions.text: the 20th century, almost all children needed to go to school with a full-time schedule.
questions.explanationHtml:
Đáp án "NOT GIVEN"

trong bài chỉ nói là cuối thế kỷ 19, khi nhắc đên childhood là sẽ nghĩ đến "schools" || việc học ko còn là đặc quyền và học sinh được EXPECTED sẽ dành phần lớn thời gian trong ngày ở lớp học

=> ko đề cập đến thế kỷ 20 + học sinh được expect chứ ko có nghĩa là cần phải đi học (need to...)

questions.text: Nowadays, children’s needs are much differentiated and categorised based on how old they are.
questions.explanationHtml:
Đáp án "True"

Trong bài: ngày càng nhiều trẻ em được xem như là 1 nhóm với những unique need, và những học sinh này được phân thành nhóm xét theo độ tuổi của họ

questionSets.contentHtml:
• What had not become a hot topic until the French historian Philippe Aries’ book caused great attention? 8
  •  According to Aries, what was the typical image of children in Western Europe during the Middle Ages 9
  • What historical event generated the need for a large number of children to work for a long time in the 18th and 19th centuries? 10
  • What bill was enacted to protect children from exploitation in Britain in the 1800s? 11
  • Which activities were becoming regarded as preferable for almost all children in the 19th century? 12
  • In what place did children spend the majority of time during their day in school? 13

câu hỏi: cái bill vào được enact (thực thi) để bảo vệ trẻ em khỏi sự bóc lột
